title: Check-off-to-purchase-log with price prompt
goal: Let checking a shopping-list item off optionally log a real purchase -- a stock_movements 'purchase' row, a price_history row, and an item_stats purchase_count/last_purchased_at bump -- with no receipt involved, so a shop trip without a photographed bill still feeds E-5's prediction engine (REQ-18's core point: 'checking off an item without a receipt still feeds the model when a price is logged'). Mirrors commit_receipt()'s (S-13) minimal item_stats bookkeeping and lib/review/commit.ts's RPC-then-recompute shape, but for exactly one item instead of a receipt's worth of lines, and deliberately skips S-15's rate_correction reconciliation (receipt-commit-only by that story's own invariants).
in_scope: Migration: alter table shopping_list_items add column purchase_logged_at timestamptz, add column logged_price numeric (both nullable, additive) -- purchase_logged_at is the one thing the existing schema cannot express: whether THIS list row already produced a ledger write, distinct from 'checked' (a bare boolean a user can toggle back and forth without touching history, ADR-0001). Also creates function log_shopping_list_purchase(p_shopping_list_item_id uuid, p_unit_price numeric) returns table(catalog_item_id uuid, household_id uuid, already_logged boolean): selects the shopping_list_items row FOR UPDATE (row lock -- this is what makes a double-click/double-submit race-safe, not just documented-and-accepted: a second concurrent call blocks on the lock, then on acquiring it sees purchase_logged_at already set by the first and takes the no-op branch). If purchase_logged_at is already set: sets checked=true (idempotent) and returns already_logged=true, no further writes. Otherwise: qty_base = coalesce(shopping_list_items.qty_base, catalog_items.default_pack_size, 1) (S-23 always populates qty_base at generation time, so this fallback is defense-in-depth, not the expected path); inserts one stock_movements row (type='purchase', qty_base, occurred_at=now(), source_receipt_id=null -- the null is load-bearing, see lib/predictions/reconcile.ts's existing comment explaining the null-source-id branch exists precisely for this); inserts one price_history row (merchant=null, unit_price=p_unit_price, observed_at=now()); upserts item_stats exactly as commit_receipt's per-line body does (insert ... on conflict (catalog_item_id) do update set purchase_count = purchase_count + 1, last_purchased_at = greatest(...), updated_at) -- same bookkeeping idiom, not reinvented; updates the shopping_list_items row itself (checked=true, purchase_logged_at=now(), logged_price=p_unit_price); returns already_logged=false.

lib/shopping-list/checkoff.ts (server-only): logShoppingListPurchase(shoppingListItemId, unitPrice) calls the RPC, and -- only when already_logged came back false (the RPC's own guard is the single source of truth for 'did this call actually write', not a second check in TypeScript) -- calls recomputeOneItem(catalogItemId, householdId) with NO rateCorrectionOverride (mirrors lib/inventory/consume.ts's recordConsumption exactly: 'S-15's reconciliation is purchase-commit-only per its own invariants and must never be reached from a consumption action' -- a checkoff-purchase is not a receipt commit either, same reasoning applies verbatim), then resets any 'snoozed' or 'skipped' plan_entries row for that item back to 'pending' (an 'excluded' row is left untouched -- that is a deliberate, stronger signal a stray purchase log must not override). setChecked(shoppingListItemId, checked: boolean): plain shopping_list_items update of the checked column only -- used for the no-price cross-off path (S-23's setCheckedAction already calls the equivalent one-column update; this story does not duplicate that, it only adds the price-logging path).

app/shopping-list/actions.ts: logPurchaseAction(shoppingListItemId, unitPrice: number) wraps logShoppingListPurchase, revalidatePath('/shopping-list' and '/plan' and '/' and '/inventory' -- a logged purchase changes predicted_next_purchase_at and cadence, visible on all four).

app/shopping-list/shopping-list-item-row.tsx ('use client'): per item, a checkbox (calls setCheckedAction, no price) and, only while purchase_logged_at is null, a small inline number input + 'Log purchase' button (calls logPurchaseAction with a positive numeric price; empty/invalid input disables the button, matching this repo's existing plain-HTML-controls convention, no new form library). Once purchase_logged_at is set, the price control is replaced with 'Logged: ₹{logged_price}' -- both the RPC's write and this display read the exact number the user entered, not a recomputed/derived one.
out_of_scope: S-15 rate_correction reconciliation on the checkoff-purchase path -- deliberately not invoked, matching recordConsumption's existing precedent and S-15's own commit-receipt-only invariant. Verified (not assumed) as part of this story's test plan that a later real receipt commit's reconciliation still correctly treats a null-source checkoff movement as a valid 'previous purchase' to compare against.

Editing or un-logging a already-logged purchase (the 'Logged: ₹X' display is read-only) -- no acceptance criterion requires reversing a logged purchase; the ledger stays an append-only audit trail (ADR-0001), consistent with S-13's own out-of-scope note.

Unchecking (setChecked(id, false)) ever touching purchase_logged_at, logged_price, or writing any reversing stock_movements row -- a checkbox toggle is list-crossing-off state only, never a ledger operation. Explicitly verified, not left to infer.
acceptance: Checking an item off without a receipt still writes a purchase movement when a price is entered.
invariants: log_shopping_list_purchase never writes stock_movements/price_history/item_stats a second time for the same shopping_list_items row -- enforced by the FOR UPDATE row lock plus the purchase_logged_at IS NULL guard inside one transaction, not by a client-side check that a concurrent double-click could race past.
logShoppingListPurchase never passes a rateCorrectionOverride to recomputeOneItem -- reconciliation stays receipt-commit-only, matching S-15's own stated scope.
setChecked (the no-price path) never inserts into stock_movements, price_history, or item_stats -- crossing an item off a list is not, by itself, evidence a purchase happened.
A plan_entries row in state='excluded' is never reset to 'pending' by a purchase log -- only 'snoozed'/'skipped' rows are, since exclusion is a deliberate, stronger user signal.
